profile.name: Sahil Khan
profile.title: AI Engineer & Backend Developer
profile.tagline: I build and ship production AI systems end-to-end — real-time voice agents, RAG pipelines, and self-hosted LLM infrastructure.
bio: I'm a software engineer working at the intersection of AI and backend systems. Right now I'm building a high-throughput, “true natural” voice-agent platform at Purple Sky Infotech — orchestrating STT/TTS engines and LLM APIs to hold real conversations at sub-second latency.

I'm drawn to the hard parts: self-hosting open-source LLMs on GPUs with vLLM, cutting inference cost without sacrificing latency, and building RAG systems that stay fast over hundreds of thousands of document chunks. I care about systems that are correct, observable, and cheap to run.

education.degree: B.E. in Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE)

experience.summary: Building a real-time, multi-tenant voice-agent platform and the LLM infrastructure behind it.
highlights: Architected the voice agent orchestration layer for the platform using Pipecat and async processing, delivering real-time conversational voice with end-to-end latency under 1500 ms and support for multiple LLM, TTS, and STT providers.

Built a high-performance RAG microservice for the voice agent platform using LangChain, Pinecone, and OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, integrated with AWS S3 for document uploads, AWS SQS queuing, and async Celery workers, serving 100,000+ chunks with retrieval latency under 300 ms.

Deployed Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct using vLLM with tool calling and Faster-Whisper large-v3 for transcription on an on-premises 8x V100 GPU server, cutting LLM development and testing costs by 90% compared to cloud providers.
Deployed and optimized open-source LLMs on RunPod GPUs (RTX 3090) with vLLM — a 40% reduction in inference cost while holding real-time latencies.
Integrated multiple telephony providers including Twilio, Plivo, and Vobiz into the voice platform, along with automated call retry handling to scale concurrent active calls by 60%+.

experience.summary: Contributed reliability and response-handling features to an open-source API client.
highlights: Built an AI-powered XML/JSON response visualizer generating HTML views of complex API response bodies similar to Postman, reaching 99.98% rendering accuracy in testing.
Added API response download features and image response rendering for REST APIs handling binary image data — 100% accurate binary image processing.
Implemented WebSocket disconnection detection with real-time UI alerts, improving platform stability.

experience.summary: Full-stack feature work on an e-commerce platform focused on performance, REST APIs, and authentication.
highlights: Worked across the full stack on an e-commerce platform: built REST APIs in Express with Postgres and a secure JWT-based authentication flow, integrating them into a React and TypeScript frontend styled with Tailwind CSS.
Optimized frontend performance and implemented Recoil-based state management, reducing initial page load times by 25% and cutting state-related bugs.
Cut average API response time by 20% for key user flows.

projects.name: HootPR
projects.tagline: AI code reviewer that reads, runs and fixes pull requests
projects.description: An AI review platform for GitHub and GitLab. Every pull request is cloned into a sealed sandbox, mapped with a code graph, scanned by static analyzers and investigated by tool-using LLM agents — then a judge model throws out anything it can't back with evidence. What survives lands on the PR as a walkthrough, inline comments with one-click fixes and a merge check. Ask it, and it writes the fix, the tests or the CI repair too.

features.title: Agentic review pipeline
features.detail: Triage → plan → investigator agents that read files, walk callers and callees, and run shell commands inside the sandbox — each capped at 8 tool calls and 60k tokens.

features.title: Built-in hallucination control
features.detail: A finding must sit inside the diff, apply cleanly as a patch and pass an LLM judge's confidence bar. Linter output is evidence for the agents, never posted raw.

features.title: Sealed, disposable sandbox
features.detail: Read-only, non-root, no capabilities, 768 MB; the network is cut after the clone and the container is destroyed after. Repo text is fenced off as untrusted input against prompt injection.

features.title: It writes the fix, too
features.detail: @hootpr autofix, generate unit tests (run and iterated until they pass), fix CI from the failed job logs, resolve merge conflicts — pushed as a commit or a stacked PR.

features.title: Security suite
features.detail: Blast radius traces changed code back to the HTTP routes it can reach; a repo-wide attack-surface map and an on-demand security architecture review.

features.title: Learns each team
features.detail: Preferences taught in the PR thread are embedded in pgvector and recalled on the next review. Linked repos, remote MCP servers and web search add context.

features.title: Dashboard with a full trace
features.detail: Every review's stages, agent steps, LLM calls, tool runs and judge verdicts; a Monaco diff workspace with findings inline; analytics, reports, audit log and a public REST API.

features.title: Measured, not guessed
features.detail: An eval suite of seeded bugs, reversed CVE fixes and clean PRs scores precision, recall and cost per PR, with ablations that switch stages off.

features.title: AWS Cloud deployment
features.detail: Deployed on AWS EC2 (small instance) with AWS RDS for PostgreSQL and pgvector.

projects.name: Assay
projects.tagline: AI equity research agent — a report card for every stock
projects.description: Type a US ticker and Assay reads the company's financials and SEC filings, computes every ratio in Python, benchmarks them against peers, and grades the business on profitability, financial health, growth, valuation and sentiment — then writes a cited investment memo with a BUY / HOLD / SELL call. The LLM writes the argument; it never produces a number and never picks the rating.

features.title: Every number is verified
features.detail: Ratios are computed in pure Python. After the memo is written, every %, multiple and dollar figure is extracted and matched against those values — a transposed digit sends it back for a rewrite.

features.title: A rubric makes the call
features.detail: 27 metrics are scored 0–10 against named anchors and folded into five weighted dimensions. The model is told the rating and argues for it; if it disagrees, that goes in the caveats.

features.title: Every claim is cited
features.detail: Qualitative sentences must cite a retrieved passage. Uncited claims, or citations to sources that don't exist, are removed before the memo is saved.

features.title: Retrieval led by the numbers
features.detail: 10-Ks streamed from SEC EDGAR plus news, chunked into pgvector. When revenue fell or leverage is high, it searches specifically for demand weakness or refinancing risk.

features.title: Peer benchmarking
features.detail: Each metric gets a percentile against comparable companies — “operating margin 31%, better than 88% of peers” — with meaningless multiples filtered out.

features.title: “What would make it a BUY?”
features.detail: The rubric runs backwards: a Scenario tab solves the smallest move in each metric that flips the rating, with draggable levers — no data fetch and no model call.

features.title: Live pipeline, full trace
features.detail: Server-sent events stream each node as it finishes; the trace tab shows tokens, cost and citation rate for every run.

features.title: AWS Cloud deployment
features.detail: Deployed on AWS EC2 (small instance) with AWS RDS for PostgreSQL and pgvector.

features.title: A complete product
features.detail: Accounts with Google sign-in, compare, watchlist, PDF export, public share links, credits via Razorpay (test mode), quotas and a daily LLM budget guard.
